html:
The Rudd Concession was a grant of mining rights signed on 30 October 1888 by Lobengula, king of the Ndebele, to agents of Cecil Rhodes, in return for a monthly payment, a thousand rifles and a steamboat.

Lobengula believed he was allowing a few men to dig for gold. The written text, which he could not read, gave them all mineral rights in his kingdom and the power to exclude others. He soon protested that he had been deceived.

Rhodes used the concession to win a royal charter for his British South Africa Company in 1889, which sent the Pioneer Column into Mashonaland the next year and ruled the country as Rhodesia.
sum: The Rudd Concession was a grant of mining rights signed on 30 October 1888 by Lobengula, king of the Ndebele, to agents of Cecil Rhodes, in return for a monthly payment, a thousand rifles and a steamboat.
